question: A small fleck of bone seen at the base of the second metatarsal on AP foot X-ray (the 'fleck sign') is pathognomonic of a Lisfranc ligament rupture and mandates urgent further imaging and operative assessment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The fleck sign is pathognomonic for Lisfranc ligament avulsion — do not dismiss it as an incidental finding. Missed Lisfranc injuries lead to midfoot collapse and chronic pain; any displacement > 2 mm requires ORIF.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The fleck sign — an avulsion fragment at the base of the second metatarsal at its articulation with the medial cuneiform — represents avulsion of the Lisfranc ligament and is pathognomonic of Lisfranc injury. CT or stress weight-bearing X-rays are required; displaced injuries need operative fixation.
